summary: You had an emergency room visit on May 30, 2026, at an out-of-network hospital. Because this was emergency care, federal law (the No Surprises Act) protects you: your cost sharing stays at in-network levels. You owe $396 total—a $250 copay plus $146 coinsurance. The hospital cannot bill you for the $1,420 difference between what they charged and what the plan allows.

lines.explanation: This was an emergency department visit on May 30, 2026. The hospital was out-of-network, but because it was emergency care, you are protected by federal law. That means your copay and coinsurance are based on in-network rates, not out-of-network rates. You owe $250 for the copay [CODE-PR-3: "a fixed dollar amount for a covered visit or service"], plus $146 coinsurance [CODE-PR-2: "your percentage share of the allowed amount"]. The hospital billed $2,400, but the plan's allowed amount is $980. The $1,420 difference is written off by the provider [CODE-CO-45: "The difference is written off by the provider. Members do not owe CO-45 amounts"]—you never owe that part.

citations.quote: The emergency room copay is $250, waived if you are admitted to the hospital.
PR-3 means this amount is a copay, a fixed dollar amount for a covered visit or service.
PR-2 means this amount is coinsurance, your percentage share of the allowed amount after the deductible is met.
CO-45 means the provider billed more than the rate they agreed to with the plan. The difference is written off by the provider. Members do not owe CO-45 amounts for in-network care.

actions: Review any bill from St. Adelaide Regional Medical Center. It should show only your $250 copay and $146 coinsurance ($396 total). If the hospital bills you for any amount above that, contact them immediately and reference this EOB and claim CLM-2026-88617.
Verify that your out-of-pocket total of $396 has been applied to your yearly out-of-pocket maximum. Your plan records show you had used $1,600 before this visit.
